children: Australian stocks are set to fall in early trade after a speech by U.S. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh was seen by investors as supporting the case for a near-term interest-rate rise. Geopolitical concerns are also elevated after U.S. forces attacked two Iranian rocket launchers in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, marking the first American strike in weeks. Local stock futures are down by 0.4% ahead of Friday's open, suggesting the S&P/ASX 200 could immediately give back the 0.4% gain it compiled last week. The benchmark index is up by 1.3% so far in August and on course for a fifth straight monthly gain. U.S. stocks provided a soft lead Friday. The DJIA was broadly flat, but the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite fell 0.25% and 0.5%, respectively. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
